source.title: Semantic Convergence: Investigating Shared Representations Across Scaled LLMs
source.authors: Daniel Son; Sanjana Rathore; Andrew Rufail; A. Simon; Daniel Zhang; S. Dave; Cole Blondin; Kevin Zhu; Sean O'Brien

record.tranche_reason: It measures cross-model feature alignment using SAE feature matching, SVCCA, RSA, and semantic-subspace comparisons. This tests representation convergence with different metrics and settings, rather than reproducing the original measurement exactly.
record.gate_note: The reported measurements of paired feature alignment, semantic-subspace alignment, and metric/subspace comparisons are included. Cited results from Lan et al. and other work are not included. The text’s figures are described in places without exact cell values; only the aggregate values or approximate values explicitly stated in the text and captions are recorded.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-model alignment of SAE features between Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B. It uses SVCCA and RSA against random-pair baselines, which directly tests V5 (universal features). It also bears on V6 (dependence on measure and inputs) and V7 (incomplete alignment). It is a follow-up to Lan et al., not an original source. It compares only one size pair, so it gives no scaling trend for V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that Gemma-2-2B and 9B share strongly aligned SAE feature spaces, mainly in middle layers, while early and late layers align much less. They add that coherent overlapping and multi-token subspaces align, but incompatible pairs do not. They frame universality as a structural property of the Gemma family, possibly extending across families when combined with Lan et al.'s Pythia results.
record.recipe_differences: Builds on Lan et al.'s SAE feature pairing approach and uses SVCCA and RSA, while applying it to Gemma-2-2B versus Gemma-2-9B and adding overlapping and multi-token semantic-subspace analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment varies across layers, feature-matching strategy (1-to-1 versus many-to-1), filtering of non-concept features, and the semantic subspaces compared. The paper reports no statistically significant changes from the tested similarity-metric substitutions.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean activation correlation of matched SAE features peaks at 0.70, rising to 0.74 after filtering. These values come from the correlation-maximising matching itself.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pairing-statistic magnitudes for matched SAE features across model sizes (a selection quantity, not a convergence measure).

record.problems: The study is limited to Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B, which share a tokenizer; the authors note that a shared tokenizer can improve pairing quality. The number of semantic subspaces is limited, and only one multi-token subspace is tested. It does not measure capability or a scaling trend across multiple sizes, and the reported similarity is layer-dependent and incomplete.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Figures with heatmaps are not expanded into per-cell rows where the text supplies no exact cell values.

untested.parts: All of it. Only one same-family, same-tokenizer pair (2B vs 9B) is compared, so there is no scaling series, capability measure, or cross-architecture or cross-objective comparison. Alignment rising with scale is not shown.
All. There are no seed replicates of one architecture; the '5 runs' are repeats of the matching procedure.
All. There is no mapping, stitching, or transfer loss.
Recurrence across different architectures, tokenizers or families; circuits.
Neighbour counts and out-of-distribution inputs (beyond 'unlikely' concatenations, which have no numbers).
Plateau with scale, and whether shared data, tokenizer or objective explains the alignment.

missing.what: Per-concept semantic-subspace SVCCA/RSA values. Captions say SVCCA peaks near 0.40 at L10–L19, several concepts exceed 0.60, and RSA peaks near 0.17. People/Roles falls below 0 at L2; Biology reaches ~0.30 and Countries ~0.25 at 9B L19.
RSA scores for overlapping subspaces (the text says these are high or low, matching SVCCA) and the other overlapping pairs (calendar-nature, calendar-people, country-time).

record.verdict_notes: V1 links were removed from all rows. Two models of one family, sharing a tokenizer, give no evidence about convergence rising with scale. The authors themselves note that a shared tokenizer improves pairing quality. The Table 2 p-value (0.02 with paired score below random) is internally inconsistent. The Table 3 caption ('bad pairs') looks copied. The '5 run mean' refers to random-procedure repeats, not model seeds.

versions.untested_parts: Only Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B are compared. The study does not measure alignment over a scaling series, establish that alignment rises with scale, measure capability, or compare independently trained models across different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No vision-language model pairs or paired images and captions are studied.
The models are not the same architecture trained from different initializations; shared features across seeds or shared subspaces across seeds are not tested.
Feature matching and representational similarity are measured, but the study does not test interchangeability, mapping loss, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
The study compares SAE-derived features in two Gemma-2 models only. It does not establish recurrence of the same features across architectures or modalities, or test circuits.
The study reports metric comparisons and effects of semantic-subspace choice, but does not test different neighbour counts or out-of-distribution inputs.

The study shows incomplete and condition-dependent alignment, but does not determine whether shared training data or objectives cause it, or compare those explanations against a common model of reality.
